sources.title: Quality Gate: Estimating the Quality of Machine Translation for Public Administration Use Cases

inspection_spans.observation: A quality gate routes acceptable MT directly and unacceptable MT to human post-editing in public-administration assimilation and dissemination use cases.
Threshold trade-offs vary by language and use case; human raters disagree in one dissemination condition and the conclusions are limited to examined cases.

sources.supports: A real decision-routing formulation linking MT quality, cost, speed, language, and use case.
sources.does_not_establish: A universal threshold or transfer to unexamined languages and settings.

sources.title: Supporting User Reliance on Machine Translation via Implicit and Explicit Feedback

inspection_spans.observation: Implicit backtranslation and question-answer feedback improve decision accuracy and appropriate reliance while preserving user agency; critical errors remain difficult.
The study is limited to English-Spanish, one COVID communication domain, one system, four feedback forms, and synthetic errors.

sources.supports: Feedback presentation can change human decisions and appropriate reliance on MT.
sources.does_not_establish: Broad language, domain, system, or natural-error generalization.

sources.title: European Commission use of eTranslation

inspection_spans.observation: The service supplies MT when human translations are unavailable, is fully automated, varies by text and language pair, and is available to public administrations.

inspection_spans.locator: Use of machine translation on Europa, lines 278-282 as inspected 2026-07-19
inspection_spans.observation: The Commission frames output as a basic idea, disclaims guaranteed accuracy, and excludes EU legislation from this use.

sources.supports: A current public workflow where raw MT is exposed under explicit fit-for-purpose limits and variable quality.
sources.does_not_establish: How often users make consequential errors, which feedback design is best, or a universal routing threshold.
